misconceptions.description: Communicating excitement or vague reassurance instead of specific data, retention, and opt-out facts
misconceptions.trigger: family letter says innovative or industry-standard but never states what data is shared or how to decline
misconceptions.feedback: State exactly what data is shared, how long it is kept, and how families can opt out, in plain language.

misconceptions.description: Offering an opt-out whose alternatives still carry the same risk being declined
misconceptions.trigger: every listed alternative uses the same login and uploads the same data
misconceptions.feedback: Provide a genuinely different option that avoids the declined risk, or the opt-out is not real consent.

misconceptions.description: Sending AI-drafted privacy claims to families without checking them against the tool's actual agreement
misconceptions.trigger: retention or training-use statements are taken from the model draft and not verified
misconceptions.feedback: Verify every data claim against the real data agreement before the memo reaches families.

misconceptions.description: Treating reading level and translation as formatting rather than as part of informed consent
misconceptions.trigger: memo is English-only at a high reading level in a multilingual or varied-literacy community
misconceptions.feedback: Make the notice comprehensible to the families it serves; consent from an unreadable notice is not informed.
